in.role: Raiders' starting tight end while Brock Bowers is out after knee surgery

out.role: Bears RB behind D'Andre Swift, hyperextended knee on Aug 16, DNP Wednesday
out.alert: ESPN still lists him ACTIVE at 10.3. He was a DNP on Wednesday and Chicago has cast doubt on his Week 1 status.

doFirst.why: Pitts keeps the tight end slot — this is the seat behind him, which you currently do not have. Mayer is the largest ownership move on either wire (+3.24) at 28.2% rostered, and the move is a real role change rather than a projection wobble: Bowers had knee surgery and misses a game or two, and Mayer starts in his place against a Miami defence reporting rates among the league's worst. SI's Week 1 tight end piece says pick him up; PFN says your current tight end is better. Both are right — take him as the seat behind Pitts, not ahead of him. On the drop, I am telling you to cut a back rostered in 78.6% of leagues and the market has this one stale: Monangai hyperextended his knee on Aug 16, was listed DNP on Wednesday, and multiple Chicago outlets spent the back half of the week casting doubt on his Week 1 status while ESPN's file still says ACTIVE at 10.3. Practice participation beats a designation. He is also your RB5 in a league whose only flex is RB/WR. Act before 17:00Z — Chicago kicks then and a locked player cannot be dropped.

doFirst.why: The second-order effect of the same injury: Bowers' surgery vacates a 30% target share and Tucker is the Raiders' main beneficiary on a shallow depth chart, in full PPR where that reception volume counts double. Allgeier is the opposite bet — LaFleur rotates his backs by policy, Rapoport reports Love is expected to play, and Arizona is a 9.5-point road dog with a 19.0 implied total, the worst script on the slate for a short-yardage specialist. Both men here are free agents and Chem's waiver order resets weekly, so neither card costs you anything lasting. If you only want to touch the bench once today, make it the Mayer card and skip this one.

trades.headline: Drake Maye is the weakest starting slot on their roster and Stafford beats him outright — they gain 0.9 a week, more than you do on paper
trades.yourSurplus: Stafford is your QB2 behind Josh Allen and you will never start him. He already played this week for 4.1 and is a dead bench seat from here to the Allen bye. Odunze is startable: SI has him a must-start receiver in Week 1 and PFN calls him a WR3 you can trust, in Chicago's 24.5-implied-total game at Carolina.
trades.theirHole: They start Drake Maye at 16.4. Stafford's 17.6 is a straight upgrade at the one slot they cannot improve from their own bench, and they are six receivers deep — Chase, London, Metcalf, Godwin, Jayden Reed — so Odunze leaves the flex without opening a hole.
trades.yourLineup: No change to your starting nine today. From next week Odunze competes with McLaurin and Brian Thomas Jr. for the RB/WR flex, which is the slot your bench currently cannot reach.
trades.theirLineup: Maye to the bench, Stafford under centre, DK Metcalf re-fills the flex.
trades.risk: Do not send it today — nobody trades a starting receiver for a quarterback who has already played his week; propose it once this slate is done and Stafford is next week's asset again. Odunze also carried a Week 1 injury question and is reported likely rather than certain to play, while the league file shows him ACTIVE, so confirm before you send. And be honest about the shape: the one-week edge to you is 0.2. The real case is positional — an unstartable backup quarterback becoming a startable receiver — and season-long value is exactly what this brief cannot price, because only weekly projections are published.

candidates.note: Mark Andrews is free here at 83.4% rostered elsewhere, which is exactly the shape the OWNED band flags as somebody's blunder. It is not one. Yahoo's 2026 outlook calls him a strong fade even if you punt tight end, and ESPN's 10.1 is the optimistic number for him rather than the pessimistic one. This row exists so you spend the bench seat on Mayer instead, whose role changed this week for a reason you can point at. Revisit Andrews only if Pitts gets hurt.

Jakobi Meyers is free at 79.4% rostered — the most valuable thing a wire can hold, a starter somebody let go. PFN's Jacksonville depth-chart reporting places him in the Jaguars' top four route runners, ahead of Travis Hunter, and Jacksonville carries a 25.0 implied total as 9.5-point favourites, the best offensive environment of the early window. He does not crack a lineup behind Jefferson, Garrett Wilson and McLaurin, so nothing is urgent — he is the first name to take if McLaurin's flex seat stops paying, and a claim costs nothing lasting here because priority resets weekly.

Trevor Lawrence is rostered in 88.3% of leagues and sits free in Chem — Guillo-tinas dropped him on Friday to add Keenan Allen. PFN has him on an eighth straight QB1 week against Cleveland. You do not need a QB2 behind Josh Allen and this is not a move for today, but Buffalo's bye is Week 7, and Lawrence is the best quarterback anyone in this league can have for nothing. If the Stafford trade lands, this is the seat that replaces him.
